description.narrative: The project will be implemented in Momzambique in Zambezia Province by Provincial Union of Small Holder Farmers of Zambezia (UPCZ). The Eco Vida project in Gurué and Milange seeks to address severe cyclical climate impacts by strengthening community resilience, improving food security, and promoting sustainable natural-resource use. It tackles interconnected issues of poverty, malnutrition, low agricultural productivity, and environmental degradation through participatory, capacity-building approaches that support inclusive, practical, and transparent climate-adaptation and mitigation strategies. R1. Stronger civil-society partner organisations; R2 Greater gender equality and women's rights; R3 Increased mobilisation and collective action by women for the right to food; R4 Enhanced community resilience, a healthier environment, and stronger climate adaptation and R5 More sustainable and secure livelihoods. The project targets 6,500 vulnerable rural residents, including men, women, boys and girls in community associations and organised local groups. Main activities include establishing community feedback mechanisms, sharing information, documenting positive social norms, and training GCB focal points in governance and leadership. The project will deliver women's economic-empowerment and value-chain training, support radio programmes, contribute to LAP development, train smallholder farmers, promote climate-smart agriculture, create early-warning systems, set up demonstration fields, seed banks and fairs, and train women in entrepreneurship.
